name: LA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+25 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold the strong default
Incumbent Troy Carter holds a large money edge; the Republican challenger shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 97 percent
No polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+25 district, an incumbent with a heavy fundraising advantage over an unfunded challenger, and markets pricing a Democratic win at 97 percent, with no contrary polling or ratings to justify moving the estimate off its fundamentals-based margin of roughly 27 points.
model.watch: Louisiana's jungle-primary format, where a runoff looms if Carter falls short of a majority, or late outside spending is the main thing that could shift the outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's second district carries a partisan lean of about 25 points toward Democrats, making it one of the safest Democratic seats on the ballot. Troy Carter, the incumbent, is running for re-election and has raised about $1.4 million, leaving him with a large financial edge. His Republican opponent, Peter Williams, shows no reported fundraising, and the ballot also includes a second Democrat and two minor-party candidates.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 97 percent. With the incumbent's money advantage and the seat's heavy Democratic lean, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with an expected margin of roughly 27 points.
